source: IBO, Analysis of the 2027 Preliminary Budget (Mar 24 2026) p.9; DOF Annual Report FY2026 p.32; OMB FY2027 Preliminary Budget summary (Feb 2026) and Executive Budget (May 2026); Comptroller, Comments on the FY2027 Adopted Budget; NY Focus May 29 2026; Chapter 59 of 2026 Part HH; Chapter 127 of 2026 Part D; Local Law 153 of 2023; General City Model section 101; see research/02-who-controls-what.md
quote_ibo: As IBO reported, the property tax is the only local tax where the City has authority to set the tax rates without State approval. The City Council, however, would have to agree to the Mayor's proposal for any change to occur.
quote_dof: Because of the property tax's unique role in balancing the budget, it is the only tax over which the City has the discretion to determine the rate without prior legislation from the State.

property_tax.who: City Hall and the City Council set the levy, the total tax billed, and the rate for each class every year.
property_tax.limits: State law set up the four property classes and the caps on yearly assessment increases, as well as the formula that sets each class's share of the tax and limits how fast a share can grow. The state constitution caps the property tax raised for operating costs, not counting debt payments, at 2.5% of the average full value of taxable property over five years. In fiscal 2026 the city was $2.2 billion under that cap, which is recalculated each year.
property_tax.alone: Raise or lower the overall rate, with the City Council's agreement. As a last resort, the mayor's February 2026 preliminary budget proposed raising the average rate 9.5%, from $12.283 to $13.450 per $100 of assessed value, worth about $3.7 billion a year. His May executive budget dropped it.

personal_income_tax.who: Albany sets the rates and must renew them periodically; the current rates run through tax year 2029.
personal_income_tax.limits: The state budget enacted in May 2026 left out the mayor's request for 2 percentage points more on incomes over $1 million, worth about $3 billion a year by the Independent Budget Office's estimate.
personal_income_tax.alone: Nothing on rates. It can adjust some credits by local law: an August 2026 law trimmed the credit residents get for unincorporated business tax, worth about $68 million in fiscal 2027.

sales_tax.who: Albany authorizes the city's 4.5% rate, and the state collects the tax and sends it to the city.
sales_tax.limits: Broadening what is taxed would take a change to state tax law. These squares also hold the mortgage recording tax, whose rates are in state law.

business_taxes.who: Albany sets the corporation and unincorporated business tax rates.
business_taxes.limits: In March 2026 the state Senate and Assembly each backed the mayor's request to let the city raise its own corporate tax rates, New York Focus reported; the state budget signed in May left it out.

other_taxes.who: Mostly Albany: the real property transfer tax is set in state law, and so are the thresholds, rates and June 2031 expiration of the new second-home surcharge, budgeted at $500 million a year.
other_taxes.limits: These squares are grayed as a group, though the hotel and commercial rent taxes in them are set by local law.
other_taxes.alone: The City Council sets the hotel tax rate by local law: it raised the rate to 5.875% in 2009 and most recently extended it through November 2027. It has also cut the commercial rent tax by local law.

fees_fines_other.who: Mostly the city and its boards: fees, fines and water and sewer charges.
